lessons.title: Key Facts
lessons.notes_html:
Facts to Remember

  • The unit of relative atomic mass is none (it is a pure ratio, dimensionless).
  • The exact masses of isotopes can be determined by mass spectrograph.
  • The phenomenon of isotopy was first discovered by Soddy.
  • Empirical formula can be determined by combustion analysis for those compounds which have carbon and hydrogen in them.
  • A limiting reagent is that which controls the quantities of the products formed. It is consumed first, and no more product can form once it is used up.
  • 1 mole of glucose has 6 x 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of carbon, 6 x 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of oxygen and 12 x 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of hydrogen, because one molecule C6H12O6 contains 6 C, 6 O and 12 H atoms.
  • Step 1 - Moles of CH4 = 4 g / 16 g mol-1 = 0.25 mol. Step 2 - Molecules = 0.25 mol x 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1 = 1.505 x 10^23 molecules of CH4.
  • Stoichiometric calculations can be performed only when the law of conservation of mass (a balanced chemical equation) is obeyed.

mcqs.q: What is the unit of relative atomic mass?
options: It has no unit, it is a pure ratio and dimensionless
mcqs.why: The notes state the unit of relative atomic mass is none because it is a pure ratio, so it is dimensionless and carries no unit at all.

mcqs.q: By which instrument can the exact masses of isotopes be determined?
mcqs.why: The key facts state that the exact masses of isotopes can be determined by mass spectrograph, which separates ions according to their mass.

mcqs.q: Who first discovered the phenomenon of isotopy?
mcqs.why: The notes record that the phenomenon of isotopy was first discovered by Soddy, so Soddy is credited with this discovery in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Empirical formula can be determined by combustion analysis for compounds containing which elements?
mcqs.why: The notes say empirical formula can be determined by combustion analysis for those compounds which have carbon and hydrogen in them.

mcqs.q: What does a limiting reagent control in a chemical reaction?
options: The colour of the products formed
The quantities of the products formed
The temperature of the reaction mixture
The speed of stirring of the mixture
mcqs.why: A limiting reagent is defined in the notes as that which controls the quantities of the products formed in a chemical reaction.

mcqs.q: What happens to the limiting reagent during a reaction?
options: It remains unused at the end
It is produced again at the end
It is consumed first and then no more product can form
It increases in amount as product forms
mcqs.why: The notes state the limiting reagent is consumed first, and no more product can form once it is used up, so the reaction stops then.

mcqs.q: How many atoms of carbon are present in 1 mole of glucose C6H12O6?
mcqs.why: One molecule of glucose contains 6 carbon atoms, so 1 mole contains 6 * 6.02 * 10^23 = 36.12 * 10^23 atoms, written in the notes as 6 x 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of carbon.

mcqs.q: How many moles are present in 4 g of CH4 if its molar mass is 16 g mol-1?
mcqs.why: Moles = mass / molar mass, so 4 / 16 = 0.25, therefore 4 g of CH4 is 0.25 mol as worked in the notes step by step.

mcqs.q: How many molecules are present in 0.25 mol of CH4?
mcqs.why: Molecules = moles * Avogadro number, so 0.25 * 6.02 = 1.505, therefore the number is 1.505 * 10^23 molecules of CH4.

mcqs.q: Stoichiometric calculations can be performed only when which condition is obeyed?
options: The law of constant colour of products
The rule that all reactants are gases
The condition that no product is formed
The law of conservation of mass, shown by a balanced chemical equation
mcqs.why: The notes state stoichiometric calculations can be performed only when the law of conservation of mass, that is a balanced chemical equation, is obeyed.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i). Isotopes differ in
✓ A. properties which depend upon mass
B. arrangement of electrons in orbitals
C. chemical properties
D. the extent to which they may be affected in electromagnetic field

Q1(ii). Select the most suitable answer: isotopes are comparatively abundant when
they have
A. even atomic masses
B. odd atomic masses
✓ C. even atomic masses and even atomic numbers
D. even atomic masses and odd atomic numbers

Q1(iii). Many elements have fractional atomic masses. This is because
A. the mass of the atom is itself fractional
B. atomic masses are average masses of isobars
C. atomic masses are average masses of isotopes
✓ D. atomic masses are average masses of isotopes proportional to their relative
abundance

Q1(iv). The mass of one mole of electrons is
A. 1.008 mg
✓ B. 0.55 mg
C. 0.184 mg
D. 1.673 mg

Q1(v). 27 g of Al will react completely with how much mass of O2 to produce Al2O3?
A. 8 g of oxygen
B. 16 g of oxygen
C. 32 g of oxygen
✓ D. 24 g of oxygen

Q1(vi). The number of moles of CO2 which contain 8.0 g of oxygen is
✓ A. 0.25
B. 0.50
C. 1.0
D. 1.50

Q1(vii). The largest number of molecules are present in
✓ A. 3.6 g of H2O
B. 4.8 g of C2H5OH
C. 2.8 g of CO
D. 5.4 g of N2O5

Q1(viii). One mole of SO2 contains
A. 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of oxygen
B. 18.1 x 10^23 molecules of SO2
✓ C. 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of sulphur
D. 4 gram atoms of SO2

Q1(ix). The volume occupied by 1.4 g of N2 at S.T.P. is
A. 2.24 dm3
B. 22.4 dm3
✓ C. 1.12 dm3
D. 112 cm3

Q1(x). A limiting reactant is the one which
A. is taken in lesser quantity in grams as compared to other reactants
B. is taken in lesser quantity in volume as compared to the other reactants
C. gives the maximum amount of the product which is required
✓ D. gives the minimum amount of the product under consideration

mcqs.q: Isotopes differ in which property?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus
mcqs.why: Isotopes have the same electron arrangement and chemical properties, but the lesson marks properties which depend upon mass as the property in which they differ.

mcqs.q: Isotopes are comparatively abundant when they have what combination?
options: Even atomic masses and even atomic numbers
Even atomic masses and odd atomic numbers
Odd atomic masses and odd atomic numbers
mcqs.why: The lesson indicates isotopes are comparatively abundant when they have even atomic masses and even atomic numbers together.

mcqs.q: Why do many elements have fractional atomic masses?
options: The mass of a single atom is itself fractional
Atomic masses are average masses of isobars
Atomic masses are average masses of isotopes proportional to their relative abundance
Every isotope has exactly the same mass
mcqs.why: The notes explain fractional atomic masses arise because atomic masses are average masses of isotopes proportional to their relative abundance.

mcqs.q: What is the mass of one mole of electrons?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives the mass of one mole of electrons as 0.55 mg, which is the marked correct value among the options listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: 27 g of Al will react completely with how much mass of O2 to produce Al2O3?
mcqs.why: For 4 Al + 3 O2 the masses are 4 * 27 = 108 for Al and 3 * 32 = 96 for O2, so for 27 g Al: 27 * 96 / 108 = 24, giving 24 g of oxygen.

mcqs.q: How many moles of CO2 contain 8.0 g of oxygen?
mcqs.why: One mole of CO2 contains 32 g of oxygen, so moles containing 8.0 g are 8 / 32 = 0.25, therefore the answer is 0.25 mol of CO2.

mcqs.q: Which sample contains the largest number of molecules?
mcqs.why: Moles decide molecule number: 3.6 / 18 = 0.2 for water, 4.8 / 46 = 0.104 for ethanol, 2.8 / 28 = 0.1 for CO, so water has the most moles and molecules.

mcqs.q: One mole of SO2 contains which quantity of sulphur atoms?
mcqs.why: Each SO2 molecule has one sulphur atom, so one mole contains 1 * 6.02 * 10^23 = 6.02 * 10^23 atoms of sulphur, as marked in the lesson.

mcqs.q: What volume is occupied by 1.4 g of N2 at S.T.P.?
mcqs.why: Moles of N2 = 1.4 / 28 = 0.05, and volume at S.T.P. = 0.05 * 22.4 = 1.12, so the volume occupied is 1.12 dm3.

mcqs.q: A limiting reactant is the one which gives what amount of product?
options: The maximum amount of the product which is required
No product at all in any case
The minimum amount of the product under consideration
mcqs.why: The lesson defines the limiting reactant as the one which gives the minimum amount of the product under consideration, because it runs out first.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: The unit of relative atomic mass is ____.
options: none, it is a pure ratio and dimensionless
mcqs.why: The fill in the blanks lesson states the unit of relative atomic mass is none, because it is a pure ratio and therefore dimensionless.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: The exact masses of isotopes can be determined by ____.
mcqs.why: The lesson fills this blank with mass spectrograph, the instrument used to determine the exact masses of isotopes of an element.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: The phenomenon of isotopy was first discovered by ____.
mcqs.why: The lesson states directly that the phenomenon of isotopy was first discovered by Soddy, so Soddy completes this blank correctly.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: Empirical formula can be determined by combustion analysis for compounds which have ____ in them.
mcqs.why: The lesson says combustion analysis determines empirical formula for those compounds which have carbon and hydrogen in them.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A limiting reagent is that which controls the quantities of ____.
mcqs.why: The completed sentence in the lesson reads that a limiting reagent controls the quantities of the products formed, and it is consumed first.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 1 mole of glucose has ____ atoms of carbon.
mcqs.why: Glucose C6H12O6 has 6 carbon atoms per molecule, so 1 mole has 6 * 6.02 = 36.12, that is 6 * 6.02 * 10^23 atoms of carbon.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 1 mole of glucose has ____ atoms of oxygen.
mcqs.why: One glucose molecule C6H12O6 contains 6 oxygen atoms, so 1 mole contains 6 * 6.02 * 10^23 atoms of oxygen as given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 1 mole of glucose has ____ atoms of hydrogen.
mcqs.why: One glucose molecule contains 12 hydrogen atoms, so 1 mole has 12 * 6.02 = 72.24, that is 12 * 6.02 * 10^23 atoms of hydrogen.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 4 g of CH4 at 0 degrees C and 1 atm has ____ molecules of CH4.
mcqs.why: Step 1: 4 / 16 = 0.25 mol of CH4. Step 2: 0.25 * 6.02 = 1.505, so the sample has 1.505 * 10^23 molecules of CH4.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: Stoichiometric calculations can be performed only when ____ is obeyed.
options: the rule of equal volumes of reactants
the law of conservation of colour
the law of conservation of mass, a balanced chemical equation
mcqs.why: The lesson completes this blank with the law of conservation of mass, shown by a balanced chemical equation, as the condition for stoichiometric calculations.

lessons.title: True or False
lessons.notes_html:
3(i). Neon has three isotopes and the fourth one with atomic mass 20.18 amu. False

3(ii). Empirical formula gives the information about the total number of atoms present in the molecule. False

3(iii). During combustion analysis Mg(ClO4)2 is employed to absorb water vapours. True

3(iv). Molecular formula is the integral multiple of empirical formula and the integral multiple can never be unity. False

3(v). The number of atoms in 1.79 g of gold and 0.023 g of sodium are equal. False

3(vi). The number of electrons in the molecules of CO and N2 are 14 each, so 1 g of each gas will have same number of electrons. True

3(vii). Avogadro's hypothesis is applicable to all types of gases i.e. ideal and non-ideal. False

3(viii). Actual yield of a chemical reaction may be greater than the theoretical yield. False

mcqs.q: True or False lesson: The statement 'Neon has three isotopes and a fourth one with atomic mass 20.18 amu' is:
options: True for all samples of neon
mcqs.why: The true or false lesson marks this neon statement as False, so neon is not correctly described as having a fourth isotope of mass 20.18 amu.

mcqs.q: The statement 'Empirical formula gives information about the total number of atoms present in the molecule' is:
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this statement False, meaning the empirical formula does not give the total number of atoms present in the molecule.

mcqs.q: During combustion analysis, which substance is employed to absorb water vapours?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks as True that during combustion analysis Mg(ClO4)2 is employed to absorb water vapours, so this is the correct absorber.

mcqs.q: The statement 'Molecular formula is an integral multiple of empirical formula and the multiple can never be unity' is:
options: True, the multiple can never be unity
True, the multiple is always two
False, molecular formula is never a multiple
False, the integral multiple can be unity
mcqs.why: The lesson marks the statement as False because the integral multiple can be unity, in which case molecular and empirical formulas are the same.

mcqs.q: The statement 'The number of atoms in 1.79 g of gold and 0.023 g of sodium are equal' is:
mcqs.why: The true or false lesson explicitly marks the claim about equal atoms in 1.79 g of gold and 0.023 g of sodium as False.

mcqs.q: How many electrons are there in each molecule of CO and of N2, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The lesson states the number of electrons in the molecules of CO and N2 are 14 each, which is the basis for the comparison that follows in the notes.

mcqs.q: The statement '1 g of CO and 1 g of N2 will have the same number of electrons' is marked in the lesson as:
mcqs.why: Because CO and N2 molecules each contain 14 electrons and have the same molar mass effect in the lesson, the statement about 1 g of each is marked True.

mcqs.q: The statement 'Avogadro hypothesis is applicable to all types of gases, ideal and non-ideal' is:
mcqs.why: The lesson marks the claim that Avogadro hypothesis is applicable to all types of gases, ideal and non-ideal, as False.

mcqs.q: The statement 'Actual yield of a chemical reaction may be greater than the theoretical yield' is:
options: True when a catalyst is used
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this statement False, meaning the actual yield of a chemical reaction may not be greater than the theoretical yield.

mcqs.q: Which pair of statements are both marked True in the lesson?
options: Empirical formula gives total atoms, and actual yield can exceed theoretical yield
Neon has a fourth isotope of 20.18 amu, and Avogadro hypothesis applies to all gases
Atoms in 1.79 g gold equal atoms in 0.023 g sodium, and the multiple can never be unity
Mg(ClO4)2 absorbs water vapours, and 1 g of CO and 1 g of N2 have the same number of electrons
mcqs.why: In the lesson the Mg(ClO4)2 statement and the CO and N2 electron statement are both marked True, while every statement in the other pairs is marked False.

lessons.title: Short Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q4. What are ions? Under what conditions are they produced?

An ion is an atom or a group of atoms that carries a net electric charge because it

has gained or lost electrons: loss of electrons gives a positive ion (cation) and gain

of electrons gives a negative ion (anion). Ions are produced when an atom is

ionised, for example by heating to a high temperature, by an electric discharge, by

radiation, by bombarding atoms with fast particles, or when an ionic compound

dissolves in water and its ions separate.

Q5(a). What are isotopes? How do you deduce the fractional atomic masses of

elements from the relative isotopic abundance? Give two examples in support of

your answer.

Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different

mass numbers, that is, the same number of protons but different numbers of

neutrons. The atomic mass of an element is the weighted average of the masses of

its isotopes: average atomic mass = sum over isotopes of (isotopic mass x

fractional abundance). Example 1 - Chlorine has Cl-35 (about 75%) and Cl-37 (about

25%), giving (35 x 0.75) + (37 x 0.25) = 35.5 amu. Example 2 - Boron has B-10 and

B-11, giving an average of about 10.81 amu, between the two isotopic masses.

Q5(b). How does a mass spectrograph show the relative abundance of an element?

In a mass spectrograph the vaporised atoms are ionised, accelerated and deflected

by a magnetic field, so that ions of different mass-to-charge ratio strike the detector

at different positions. Each isotope gives a separate peak at its own mass, and the

height (intensity) of each peak is proportional to the number of ions of that isotope,

that is, to its relative abundance. The relative peak heights therefore read off the

relative abundances directly.

Q5(c). What is the justification of two strong peaks in the mass spectrum for bromine,

while for iodine only one peak at 127 amu is indicated?

Bromine occurs naturally as two isotopes of almost equal abundance, Br-79 and

Br-81, so its mass spectrum shows two strong peaks of nearly equal height at 79

and 81 amu. Iodine, by contrast, is monoisotopic in nature: practically all iodine

atoms are I-127, so only one peak, at 127 amu, appears.

Q6. Silver has atomic number 47 and has 16 known isotopes but two occur naturally

i.e. Ag-107 and Ag-109. Given the mass spectrometric data (Ag-107: 106.90509

amu, 51.84%; Ag-109: 108.90476 amu, 48.16%), calculate the average atomic

mass of silver.

Step 1 - Convert the percentage abundances to fractions: Ag-107 = 0.5184, Ag-109

= 0.4816.

Step 2 - Contribution of Ag-107 = 106.90509 amu x 0.5184 = 55.4196 amu.

Step 3 - Contribution of Ag-109 = 108.90476 amu x 0.4816 = 52.4485 amu.

Step 4 - Average atomic mass = 55.4196 + 52.4485 = 107.868 amu.

Answer: 107.87 amu (book prints 107.88 amu; the difference is rounding of the

isotopic masses).

Q7. Boron with atomic number 5 has two naturally occurring isotopes. Calculate the

percentage abundance of 10B and 11B from: average atomic mass of boron = 10.81

amu; isotopic mass of 10B = 10.0129 amu; isotopic mass of 11B = 11.0093 amu.

Step 1 - Let the percentage of 10B be x. Then the percentage of 11B is (100 - x).

Step 2 - Average mass equation: [10.0129 x + 11.0093 (100 - x)] / 100 = 10.81.

Step 3 - Multiply out: 10.0129x + 1100.93 - 11.0093x = 1081.

Step 4 - Collect terms: -0.9964x = 1081 - 1100.93 = -19.93.

Step 5 - x = 19.93 / 0.9964 = 20.00.

Answer: 10B = 20.00%, 11B = 80.00% (book prints 20.002% and 79.998%; the

difference is rounding).

Q8. Define the following terms and give three examples of each: (i) Gram atom (ii)

Gram molecular mass (iii) Gram formula (iv) Gram ion (v) Molar volume (vi)

Avogadro's number (vii) Stoichiometry (viii) Percentage yield.

(i) Gram atom: the mass in grams of one mole of atoms, numerically equal to the

atomic mass; e.g. 12 g of carbon, 16 g of oxygen, 23 g of sodium. (ii) Gram

molecular mass: the mass in grams of one mole of molecules, numerically equal to

the molecular mass; e.g. 18 g of H2O, 32 g of O2, 44 g of CO2. (iii) Gram formula:

the mass in grams of one mole of formula units of an ionic compound, numerically

equal to its formula mass; e.g. 58.5 g of NaCl, 100 g of CaCO3, 98 g of H2SO4 (as

formula mass). (iv) Gram ion: the mass in grams of one mole of ions; e.g. 23 g of

Na+, 35.5 g of Cl-, 16 g of O2-. (v) Molar volume: the volume occupied by one mole

of a gas at a stated temperature and pressure; e.g. 22.414 dm3 at S.T.P., 24 dm3 at

room temperature and pressure. (vi) Avogadro's number: 6.02 x 10^23, the number

of particles in one mole of any substance. (vii) Stoichiometry: the study of the

quantitative (mole and mass) relationships between reactants and products in a

balanced chemical equation. (viii) Percentage yield: (actual yield / theoretical yield)

x 100, the efficiency of a reaction.

Q9. Justify: (a) 23 g of sodium and 238 g of uranium have equal number of atoms in

them. (b) Mg atom is twice heavier than that of carbon atom. (c) 180 g of glucose

and 342 g of sucrose have the same number of molecules but different number of

atoms present in them. (d) 4.9 g of H2SO4 when completely ionized in water, have

equal number of positive and negative charges but the number of positively

charged ions are twice the number of negatively charged ions. (e) One mg of

K2CrO4 has thrice the number of ions than the number of formula units when

ionized in water. (f) Two grams of H2, 16 g of CH4 and 44 g of CO2 occupy

separately the volumes of 22.414 dm3, although the sizes and masses of molecules

of three gases are very different from each other.

(a) 23 g Na = 23/23 = 1 mol and 238 g U = 238/238 = 1 mol, so both contain 6.02 x

10^23 atoms. (b) Atomic mass of Mg is 24 and of C is 12, so one Mg atom is 24/12

= 2 times heavier than one C atom. (c) 180 g glucose (molar mass 180) = 1 mol

and 342 g sucrose (molar mass 342) = 1 mol, so both have the same number of

molecules; but a glucose molecule has 24 atoms while a sucrose molecule has 45

atoms, so the total atom counts differ. (d) 4.9 g H2SO4 = 4.9/98 = 0.05 mol, giving

0.10 mol H+ ions and 0.05 mol SO4(2-) ions: the positive ions are twice as many in

number, but their total charge (+0.10) equals the total negative charge (-0.10). (e)

One formula unit K2CrO4 gives three ions (2 K+ and 1 CrO4(2-)) on ionisation, so

the number of ions is three times the number of formula units. (f) Each sample is 1

mol of gas (2/2, 16/16, 44/44), and by Avogadro's hypothesis equal moles of gases

occupy equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure, 22.414 dm3 at S.T.P.,

whatever the size or mass of the molecules.

Q10. Calculate each of the following quantities. (a) Mass in grams of 2.74 moles of

KMnO4. (b) Moles of O atoms in 9.00 g of Mg(NO3)2. (c) Number of O atoms in

10.037 g of CuSO4.5H2O. (d) Mass in kilograms of 2.6 x 10^20 molecules of SO2.

(e) Moles of Cl atoms in 0.822 g of C2H2Cl2. (f) Mass in grams of 5.136 moles of

Ag2CO3. (g) Mass in grams of 2.78 x 10^21 molecules of CrO2Cl2. (h) Number of

moles and formula units in 100 g of KClO3. (i) Number of K+ ions, ClO3- ions, Cl

atoms and O atoms in (h).

Step 1 (a) - Molar mass of KMnO4 = 158 g mol-1. Mass = 2.74 mol x 158 g mol-1 =

432.92 g.

Step 2 (b) - Molar mass of Mg(NO3)2 = 148 g mol-1. Moles of compound = 9.00/148

= 0.0608 mol. Each formula unit has 6 O atoms, so moles of O atoms = 0.0608 x 6

= 0.36 mol.

Step 3 (c) - Molar mass of CuSO4.5H2O = 249.68 g mol-1. Moles = 10.037/249.68 =

0.0402 mol. Each formula unit has 9 O atoms (4 + 5), so O atoms = 0.0402 x 9 x

6.02 x 10^23 = 2.18 x 10^23 atoms.

Step 4 (d) - Moles of SO2 = 2.6 x 10^20 / 6.02 x 10^23 = 4.32 x 10^-4 mol. Mass =

4.32 x 10^-4 mol x 64 g mol-1 = 0.0276 g = 2.76 x 10^-5 kg. (Book prints 2.70 x

10^-5 kg; recomputation gives 2.76 x 10^-5 kg - flagged.)

Step 5 (e) - Molar mass of C2H2Cl2 = 97 g mol-1. Moles of compound = 0.822/97 =

0.00847 mol. Each molecule has 2 Cl atoms, so moles of Cl atoms = 0.0169 mol.

(Book prints 0.0178 mol. RE-CHECKED by Worker B5 at 300 dpi, book p. 27: the

printed mass reads 0.822 g, not 0.862 g, so the book's printed answer does not

follow from its own question; 0.0169 mol is the correct value for the printed mass.)

Step 6 (f) - Molar mass of Ag2CO3 = 275.75 g mol-1. Mass = 5.136 mol x 275.75 g

mol-1 = 1416.2 g.

Step 7 (g) - Moles of CrO2Cl2 = 2.78 x 10^21 / 6.02 x 10^23 = 0.00462 mol. Mass

= 0.00462 mol x 155 g mol-1 = 0.7158 g.

Step 8 (h) - Molar mass of KClO3 = 122.55 g mol-1. Moles = 100/122.55 = 0.816

mol. Formula units = 0.816 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 4.91 x 10^23.

Step 9 (i) - Each formula unit gives 1 K+, 1 ClO3-, 1 Cl atom and 3 O atoms. Hence

K+ ions = 4.91 x 10^23, ClO3- ions = 4.91 x 10^23, Cl atoms = 4.91 x 10^23, O

atoms = 3 x 4.91 x 10^23 = 1.47 x 10^24.

Answer: (a) 432.92 g (b) 0.36 mol (c) 2.18 x 10^23 atoms (d) 2.76 x 10^-5 kg (e)

0.0169 mol (f) 1416.2 g (g) 0.7158 g (h) 0.816 mol, 4.91 x 10^23 formula units (i)

as in Step 9.

Q11. Aspartame, the artificial sweetner, has molecular formula C14H18N2O5. (a)

What is the mass of one mole of aspartame? (b) How many moles are present in 52

g of aspartame? (c) What is the mass in grams of 10.122 moles of aspartame? (d)

How many hydrogen atoms are present in 2.43 g of aspartame?

Step 1 (a) - Molar mass = (14 x 12) + (18 x 1) + (2 x 14) + (5 x 16) = 168 + 18 +

28 + 80 = 294 g mol-1.

Step 2 (b) - Moles in 52 g = 52/294 = 0.177 mol.

Step 3 (c) - Mass of 10.122 mol = 10.122 mol x 294 g mol-1 = 2975.87 g.

Step 4 (d) - Moles in 2.43 g = 2.43/294 = 0.00827 mol. Each molecule has 18 H

atoms, so moles of H atoms = 0.00827 x 18 = 0.1488 mol. Number of H atoms =

0.1488 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 8.96 x 10^22.

Answer: (a) 294 g mol-1 (b) 0.177 mol (c) 2975.87 g (d) 8.96 x 10^22 atoms of H.

Q12. A sample of 0.600 moles of a metal M reacts completely with excess of fluorine

to form 46.8 g of MF2. (a) How many moles of F are present in the sample of MF2

that forms? (b) Which element is represented by the symbol M?

Step 1 - The reaction is M + F2 → MF2, so 0.600 mol of M gives 0.600 mol of MF2.

Step 2 (a) - Each MF2 has 2 F atoms, so moles of F = 0.600 x 2 = 1.2 mol.

Step 3 (b) - Molar mass of MF2 = 46.8 g / 0.600 mol = 78 g mol-1.

Step 4 - Mass of M = 78 - (2 x 19) = 78 - 38 = 40 g mol-1.

Answer: (a) 1.2 moles of F (b) Calcium (atomic mass 40).

Q13. In each pair, choose the larger of the indicated quantity, or state if the samples

are equal. (a) Individual particles: 0.4 mole of oxygen molecules or 0.4 mole of

oxygen atoms. (b) Mass: 0.4 mole of ozone molecules or 0.4 mole of oxygen atoms.

(c) Mass: 0.6 mole of C2H2 or 0.6 mole of I2. (d) Individual particles: 4.0 g N2O4 or

3.3 g SO2. (e) Total ions: 2.3 moles of NaClO3 or 2.0 moles of MgCl2. (f) Molecules:

11.0 g H2O or 11.0 g H2O2. (g) Na+ ion: 0.500 moles of NaBr or 0.0145 kg of NaCl.

(h) Mass: 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of 235U or 6.02 x 10^23 atoms of 238U.

Step 1 (a) - Both are 0.4 mol of particles, so both contain 0.4 x 6.02 x 10^23

particles. Answer: Both are equal.

Step 2 (b) - Mass of ozone = 0.4 x 48 = 19.2 g; mass of oxygen atoms = 0.4 x 16 =

6.4 g. Answer: Ozone.

Step 3 (c) - Mass of C2H2 = 0.6 x 26 = 15.6 g; mass of I2 = 0.6 x 254 = 152.4 g.

Answer: I2.

Step 4 (d) - Moles of N2O4 = 4.0/92 = 0.0435 mol; moles of SO2 = 3.3/64 = 0.0516

mol. Answer: SO2.

Step 5 (e) - NaClO3 gives 2 ions per unit: 2.3 x 2 = 4.6 mol of ions. MgCl2 gives 3

ions per unit: 2.0 x 3 = 6.0 mol of ions. Answer: MgCl2.

Step 6 (f) - Moles of H2O = 11.0/18 = 0.611 mol; moles of H2O2 = 11.0/34 = 0.324

mol. Answer: H2O.

Step 7 (g) - NaBr gives 0.500 mol of Na+ ions. NaCl mass = 0.0145 kg = 14.5 g,

giving 14.5/58.5 = 0.248 mol of Na+ ions. Answer: NaBr.

Step 8 (h) - 6.02 x 10^23 atoms is 1 mol in each case: mass of 235U = 235 g, mass

of 238U = 238 g. Answer: 238U.

Q14. (a) Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in the four important fertilizers i.e. (i)

NH3 (ii) NH2CONH2 (urea) (iii) (NH4)2SO4 (iv) NH4NO3. (b) Calculate the

percentage of nitrogen and phosphorus in each of the following: (i) NH4H2PO4 (ii)

(NH4)2HPO4 (iii) (NH4)3PO4.

Step 1 (a)(i) - NH3 molar mass = 17. N% = 14/17 x 100 = 82.35%.

Step 2 (a)(ii) - Urea NH2CONH2 molar mass = 60. N% = 28/60 x 100 = 46.67%.

Step 3 (a)(iii) - (NH4)2SO4 molar mass = 132. N% = 28/132 x 100 = 21.21%.

Step 4 (a)(iv) - NH4NO3 molar mass = 80. N% = 28/80 x 100 = 35%.

Step 5 (b)(i) - NH4H2PO4 molar mass = 115. N% = 14/115 x 100 = 12.17%. P% =

31/115 x 100 = 26.96%.

Step 6 (b)(ii) - (NH4)2HPO4 molar mass = 132. N% = 28/132 x 100 = 21.21%. P% =

31/132 x 100 = 23.48%.

Step 7 (b)(iii) - (NH4)3PO4 molar mass = 149. N% = 42/149 x 100 = 28.18%. P% =

31/149 x 100 = 20.81%.

Answer: (a) 82.35%, 46.67%, 21.21%, 35% (b) (i) N = 12.17%, P = 26.96% (ii) N =

21.21%, P = 23.48% (iii) N = 28.18%, P = 20.81%. All match the book's printed

answers.

Q15. Glucose C6H12O6 is the most important nutrient in the cell for generating

chemical potential energy. Calculate the mass % of each element in glucose and

determine the number of C, H and O atoms in 10.5 g of the sample.

Step 1 - Molar mass of glucose = (6 x 12) + (12 x 1) + (6 x 16) = 72 + 12 + 96 =

180 g mol-1.

Step 2 - C% = 72/180 x 100 = 40%. H% = 12/180 x 100 = 6.66%. O% = 96/180 x

100 = 53.33%.

Step 3 - Moles in 10.5 g = 10.5/180 = 0.05833 mol.

Step 4 - C atoms = 0.05833 x 6 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 2.107 x 10^23.

Step 5 - H atoms = 0.05833 x 12 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 4.214 x 10^23.

Step 6 - O atoms = 0.05833 x 6 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 2.107 x 10^23.

Answer: C = 40%, H = 6.66%, O = 53.33%; C = 2.107 x 10^23, H = 4.214 x 10^23,

O = 2.107 x 10^23 atoms. Matches the book's printed answers.

Q16. Ethylene glycol is used as automobile antifreeze. It has 38.7% carbon, 9.7%

hydrogen and 51.6% oxygen. Its molar mass is 62.1 grams mol-1. Determine its

empirical formula.

Step 1 - Take 100 g of the compound: it contains 38.7 g C, 9.7 g H and 51.6 g O.

Step 2 - Moles: C = 38.7/12 = 3.225 mol; H = 9.7/1 = 9.7 mol; O = 51.6/16 = 3.225

mol.

Step 3 - Divide by the smallest (3.225): C = 1, H = 3.01 (about 3), O = 1.

Answer: Empirical formula CH3O (book prints C H3 O).

Q17. Serotonin (molar mass = 176 g mol-1) is a compound that conducts nerve

impulses in brain and muscles. It contains 68.2% C, 6.86% H, 15.09% N and 9.08%

O. What is its molecular formula?

Step 1 - Take 100 g: moles C = 68.2/12 = 5.683; H = 6.86/1 = 6.86; N = 15.09/14 =

1.078; O = 9.08/16 = 0.5675.

Step 2 - Divide by the smallest (0.5675): C = 10.01 (about 10), H = 12.09 (about

12), N = 1.90 (about 2), O = 1.

Step 3 - Empirical formula = C10H12N2O. Empirical formula mass = (10 x 12) + (12

x 1) + (2 x 14) + 16 = 176 g mol-1.

Step 4 - n = molar mass / empirical formula mass = 176/176 = 1.

Answer: Molecular formula C10H12N2O (matches the book's printed answer).

Q18. An unknown metal M reacts with S to form a compound with a formula M2S3. If

3.12 g of M reacts with exactly 2.88 g of sulphur, what are the names of metal M

and the compound M2S3?

Step 1 - Moles of sulphur = 2.88 g / 32 g mol-1 = 0.09 mol of S atoms.

Step 2 - In M2S3 the ratio M:S is 2:3, so moles of M = 0.09 x (2/3) = 0.06 mol.

Step 3 - Atomic mass of M = 3.12 g / 0.06 mol = 52 g mol-1.

Step 4 - The element with atomic mass 52 is chromium.

Answer: Metal M is chromium (Cr); the compound is chromium(III) sulphide, Cr2S3

(matches the book's printed answer).

Q19. The octane present in gasoline burns according to: 2C8H18(l) + 25O2(g) ->

16CO2(g) + 18H2O(l). (a) How many moles of O2 are needed to react fully with 4

moles of octane? (b) How many moles of CO2 can be produced from one mole of

octane? (c) How many moles of water are produced by the combustion of 6 moles of

octane? (d) If this reaction is to be used to synthesize 8 moles of CO2, how many

grams of oxygen are needed? How many grams of octane will be used?

Step 1 (a) - From the equation, 2 mol octane need 25 mol O2. For 4 mol octane: 4 x

(25/2) = 50 mol of O2.

Step 2 (b) - 2 mol octane give 16 mol CO2, so 1 mol octane gives 16/2 = 8 mol of

CO2.

Step 3 (c) - 2 mol octane give 18 mol H2O, so 6 mol octane give 6 x (18/2) = 54 mol

of H2O.

Step 4 (d) - 16 mol CO2 come from 2 mol octane, so 8 mol CO2 come from 1 mol

octane = 114 g of octane. Oxygen needed = 1 x (25/2) = 12.5 mol = 12.5 x 32 =

400 g.

Answer: (a) 50 moles (b) 8 moles (c) 54 moles (d) 400 g of oxygen, 114 g of octane.

All match the book's printed answers.

Q20. Calculate the number of grams of Al2S3 which can be prepared by the reaction

of 20 g of Al and 30 g of sulphur. How much the non-limiting reactant is in excess?

Step 1 - Balanced equation: 2Al + 3S → Al2S3.

Step 2 - Moles of Al = 20/27 = 0.741 mol. Moles of S = 30/32 = 0.9375 mol.

Step 3 - Sulphur needed for all the aluminium = 0.741 x (3/2) = 1.111 mol, which is

more than the 0.9375 mol available. Sulphur is therefore the limiting reactant and

aluminium is in excess.

Step 4 - Moles of Al2S3 formed = 0.9375/3 = 0.3125 mol. Mass = 0.3125 x 150 =

46.87 g.

Step 5 - Aluminium used = 0.9375 x (2/3) = 0.625 mol = 0.625 x 27 = 16.875 g.

Aluminium in excess = 20 - 16.875 = 3.125 g.

Answer: 46.87 g of Al2S3; 3.125 g of aluminium in excess (matches the book's

printed answers).

Q21. A mixture of two liquids, hydrazine N2H4 and N2O4, are used in rockets. They

produce N2 and water vapours. How many grams of N2 gas will be formed by

reacting 100 g of N2H4 and 200 g of N2O4?

Step 1 - Balanced equation: 2N2H4 + N2O4 → 3N2 + 4H2O.

Step 2 - Moles of N2H4 = 100/32 = 3.125 mol. Moles of N2O4 = 200/92 = 2.174

mol.

Step 3 - N2O4 needed for all the hydrazine = 3.125/2 = 1.5625 mol, which is less

than the 2.174 mol available. Hydrazine is therefore the limiting reactant.

Step 4 - Moles of N2 formed = 3.125 x (3/2) = 4.6875 mol. Mass = 4.6875 x 28 =

131.25 g.

Answer: About 131 g of N2 (book prints 131.04 g; the small difference is the

rounding of atomic masses).

Q22. Silicon carbide (SiC) is an important ceramic material. It is produced by allowing

sand (SiO2) to react with carbon at high temperature: SiO2 + 3C → SiC + 2CO.

When 100 kg sand is reacted with excess of carbon, 51.4 kg of SiC is produced.

What is the percentage yield of SiC?

Step 1 - Moles of SiO2 = 100 kg / 60 kg kmol-1 = 1.667 kmol.

Step 2 - From the equation, 1 mol SiO2 gives 1 mol SiC, so theoretical moles of SiC

= 1.667 kmol.

Step 3 - Theoretical mass of SiC = 1.667 kmol x 40 kg kmol-1 = 66.67 kg.

Step 4 - Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100 = (51.4/66.67) x

100 = 77.1%.

Answer: 77% (matches the book's printed answer).

Q23(a). What is stoichiometry? Give its assumptions?
Mention two important laws,

which help to perform the stoichiometric calculations?

Stoichiometry is the study of the quantitative relationships between reactants and

products in a chemical reaction, worked out from the balanced chemical equation.

Its assumptions are: (1) the reaction goes to completion as written, (2) all reactants

and products are pure, and (3) the equation is balanced so that atoms are

conserved. The two laws that make stoichiometric calculations possible are the law

of conservation of mass and the law of definite proportions (together with

Avogadro's hypothesis for gases).

Q23(b). What is a limiting reactant?
How does it control the quantity of the product

formed? Explain with three examples?

A limiting reactant is the reactant that is used up first in a reaction and therefore

limits how much product can form; once it is finished, the reaction stops even if

other reactants remain. It controls the product quantity because the product moles

are fixed by the limiting reactant's moles through the mole ratio of the balanced

equation. Examples: (1) In 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, hydrogen in short supply limits the

water formed. (2) In Q.20 above, sulphur limits the Al2S3 formed from aluminium

and sulphur. (3) In Q.21 above, hydrazine limits the nitrogen gas formed from

hydrazine and N2O4.

Q24(a). Define yield. How do we calculate the percentage yield of a chemical

reaction?

Yield is the amount of product actually obtained from a chemical reaction. The

theoretical yield is the amount predicted by the balanced equation if the reaction

went to completion. Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100. It is

always 100% or less in practice, because of incomplete reactions, side reactions

and losses during separation.

Q24(b). What are the factors which are mostly responsible for the low yield of the

products in chemical reactions?

Low yields are mostly caused by: (1) the reaction not going to completion

(reversible reactions reach equilibrium); (2) side reactions that consume reactants

to give unwanted products; (3) loss of product during separation, filtration, washing

and transfer; (4) impure reactants; and (5) unfavourable conditions of temperature,

pressure or catalyst.

Q25. Explain the following with reasons: (i) Law of conservation of mass has to be

obeyed during stoichiometric calculations. (ii) Many chemical reactions taking place

in our surrounding involve the limiting reactants. (iii) No individual neon atom in the

sample of the element has a mass of 20.18 amu. (iv) One mole of H2SO4 should

completely react with two moles of NaOH. How does Avogadro's number help to

explain it? (v) One mole of H2O has two moles of bonds, three moles of atoms, ten

moles of electrons and twenty eight moles of the total fundamental particles

present in it. (vi) N2 and CO have the same number of electrons, protons and

neutrons.

(i) Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass

of reactants must equal the total mass of products; stoichiometric calculations use

this to balance equations and to relate masses. (ii) In everyday reactions the

reactants are rarely mixed in exact stoichiometric proportions, and one of them (for

example oxygen from the air, or one ingredient) runs out first, so that reactant

limits the reaction. (iii) 20.18 amu is the weighted average atomic mass of neon's

isotopes (Ne-20, Ne-21, Ne-22); no single neon atom has that mass, each atom has

mass 20, 21 or 22 amu. (iv) H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O: one mole of acid

supplies 2 moles of H+ ions, which need 2 moles of OH- ions; Avogadro's number

converts these mole ratios into equal numbers of particles (2 x 6.02 x 10^23 of

each). (v) One H2O molecule has 2 O-H bonds, 3 atoms (2 H + 1 O), 10 electrons (2

+ 8) and 28 fundamental particles (10 protons + 8 neutrons + 10 electrons,

counting H: 1 proton each and O: 8 protons + 8 neutrons); one mole multiplies each

count by Avogadro's number. (vi) N2 has 14 protons, 14 electrons and 14 neutrons

(7 + 7 each); CO has 6 + 8 = 14 protons, 14 electrons and 6 + 8 = 14 neutrons, so

both molecules have the same counts.

mcqs.q: An atom or group of atoms that has lost electrons becomes which type of ion?
mcqs.why: The notes define loss of electrons as giving a positive ion called a cation, while gain of electrons gives a negative ion called an anion.

mcqs.q: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different what?
options: Mass numbers, because they have different numbers of neutrons
mcqs.why: The notes define isotopes as atoms with the same atomic number but different mass numbers, that is the same protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Chlorine has Cl-35 at about 75 percent and Cl-37 at about 25 percent. What is its average atomic mass?
mcqs.why: Average = 35 * 0.75 + 37 * 0.25 = 26.25 + 9.25 = 35.5, so the average atomic mass of chlorine is 35.5 amu as in the notes.

mcqs.q: Why does bromine show two strong peaks in its mass spectrum?
options: It has only one isotope at 127 amu
It has three isotopes of equal abundance
Its atoms all have mass 80 amu
It has two isotopes Br-79 and Br-81 of almost equal abundance
mcqs.why: The notes explain bromine occurs as Br-79 and Br-81 of almost equal abundance, so two strong peaks of nearly equal height appear at 79 and 81 amu.

mcqs.q: Why does iodine show only one peak at 127 amu in its mass spectrum?
options: Iodine has two equal isotopes at 79 and 81
Practically all iodine atoms are I-127, it is monoisotopic in nature
Iodine has no isotopes at all
mcqs.why: The notes state iodine is monoisotopic in nature, practically all its atoms are I-127, so only one peak at 127 amu appears in the spectrum.

mcqs.q: Silver isotopes Ag-107 (51.84 percent) and Ag-109 (48.16 percent) give an average atomic mass of about:
From an average atomic mass of 10.81 amu, the percentage abundance of 10B in boron is calculated as:
mcqs.why: Solving the average mass equation gives x = 19.93 / 0.9964 = 20.00, so 10B is 20.00 percent and 11B is 100 - 20 = 80.00 percent.

mcqs.q: What is Avogadro number, the number of particles in one mole of any substance?
mcqs.why: The notes define Avogadro number as 6.02 x 10^23, the number of particles in one mole of any substance, used in all mole calculations.

mcqs.q: What is the molar volume of a gas at S.T.P. given in the notes?
mcqs.why: The notes list molar volume examples as 22.414 dm3 at S.T.P. and 24 dm3 at room temperature and pressure, so 22.414 dm3 is the S.T.P. value.

mcqs.q: Why is a magnesium atom twice as heavy as a carbon atom?
options: Atomic mass of Mg is 12 and of C is 24
Mg has twice the atomic number of oxygen
Atomic mass of Mg is 24 and of C is 12, and 24 / 12 = 2
mcqs.why: The notes justify this with atomic masses: 24 / 12 = 2, so one Mg atom is two times heavier than one carbon atom.

lessons.title: Key Facts
lessons.notes_html:
Facts to Remember

  • A complete chemical characterization of a compound must include both qualitative and quantitative analyses.
  • During filtration the tip of the stem of the funnel should touch the side of the beaker to avoid splashing.
  • A fluted filter paper is used to speed up the process of filtration.
  • A solvent used for crystallization is required to dissolve a large amount of the substance at its boiling point and only a small amount at room temperature, so that crystals separate on cooling.
  • Repeated solvent extractions using small portions of solvent are more efficient than using a single extraction with larger volume of the solvent.

mcqs.q: A complete chemical characterization of a compound must include which analyses?
mcqs.why: The key facts state a complete chemical characterization of a compound must include both qualitative and quantitative analyses together.

mcqs.q: Is qualitative analysis alone enough for complete chemical characterization of a compound?
options: Yes, qualitative analysis alone is complete
No, quantitative analysis is also required
Yes, if the compound is coloured
Yes, if the compound is a solid
mcqs.why: Because the notes require both qualitative and quantitative analyses for a complete characterization, qualitative analysis alone is not enough.

mcqs.q: Is quantitative analysis alone enough for complete chemical characterization of a compound?
options: Yes, quantitative analysis alone is complete
Yes, if the mass is measured accurately
No, qualitative analysis is also required
mcqs.why: The notes make both analyses necessary for complete characterization, so quantitative analysis on its own does not complete the characterization.

mcqs.q: During filtration, where should the tip of the stem of the funnel touch?
options: The centre of the beaker base
The surface of the filter paper
The rim of the funnel itself
mcqs.why: The key facts state that during filtration the tip of the stem of the funnel should touch the side of the beaker, following the stated technique.

mcqs.q: Why should the funnel stem tip touch the side of the beaker during filtration?
mcqs.why: The notes give the reason directly: the tip touches the side of the beaker to avoid splashing of the filtrate during filtration.

mcqs.q: What is a fluted filter paper used for in filtration?
options: To speed up the process of filtration
mcqs.why: The key facts state a fluted filter paper is used to speed up the process of filtration, because its folded shape gives a larger effective area.

mcqs.q: A solvent for crystallization should dissolve how much substance at its boiling point?
options: Only a small amount of the substance
Exactly the same as at room temperature
A large amount of the substance
mcqs.why: The notes require the crystallization solvent to dissolve a large amount of the substance at its boiling point, so a hot saturated solution can form.

mcqs.q: A solvent for crystallization should dissolve how much substance at room temperature?
options: Only a small amount of the substance
A large amount of the substance
More than at its boiling point
mcqs.why: The notes require only a small amount to dissolve at room temperature, which is the opposite behaviour to that at the boiling point of the solvent.

mcqs.q: Why does a good crystallization solvent dissolve little at room temperature but much at boiling point?
options: So that the solvent evaporates at once
So that crystals separate on cooling the hot solution
So that no crystals ever form
mcqs.why: The notes explain that with this solubility difference, crystals separate on cooling because far less substance can stay dissolved at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Which way of solvent extraction is more efficient according to the key facts?
options: A single extraction with a larger volume of solvent
Heating a single extraction for longer
Repeated extractions using small portions of solvent
mcqs.why: The key facts state repeated solvent extractions using small portions of solvent are more efficient than a single extraction with a larger volume.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i). A filtration process could be very time consuming if it were not aided by a
gentle suction which is developed
A. if the paper covers the funnel upto its circumference
B. if the paper has got small sized pores in it
C. if the stem of the funnel is large so that it dips into the filtrate
✓ D. if the paper fits tightly

Q1(ii). During the process of crystallization, the hot saturated solution
✓ A. is cooled very slowly to get large sized crystals
B. is cooled at a moderate rate to get medium sized crystals
C. is evaporated to get the crystals of the product
D. is mixed with an immiscible liquid to get the pure crystals of the product

Q1(iii). Solvent extraction is an equilibrium process and it is controlled by
A. law of mass action
B. the amount of solvent used
✓ C. distribution law
D. the amount of solute

Q1(iv). Solvent extraction method is a particularly useful technique for separation
when the product to be separated is
✓ A. non-volatile or thermally unstable
B. volatile or thermally stable
C. non-volatile or thermally stable
D. volatile or thermally unstable

Q1(v). The comparative rates at which the solutes move in paper chromatography,
depend on
A. the size of paper
✓ B. Rf values of solutes
C. temperature of the experiment
D. size of the chromatographic tank used

mcqs.q: Filtration could be very time consuming if it were not aided by what?
mcqs.why: The lesson states a filtration process could be very time consuming if it were not aided by a gentle suction developed during the process.

mcqs.q: A gentle suction in filtration is developed when what condition holds?
options: The paper covers the funnel up to its circumference
The stem of the funnel is large so that it dips into the filtrate
The paper has small sized pores in it
The paper fits tightly on the funnel
mcqs.why: The marked answer in the lesson is that suction develops if the stem of the funnel is large so that it dips into the filtrate.

mcqs.q: During crystallization, how is the hot saturated solution treated to get large sized crystals?
options: It is cooled at a moderate rate
It is mixed with an immiscible liquid
mcqs.why: The lesson marks that during crystallization the hot saturated solution is cooled very slowly to get large sized crystals of the product.

mcqs.q: Cooling a hot saturated solution very slowly during crystallization gives crystals of what size?
mcqs.why: The correct option in the lesson links cooling very slowly with large sized crystals, while a moderate rate is linked with medium sized crystals.

mcqs.q: Solvent extraction is an equilibrium process controlled by which law?
mcqs.why: The lesson states solvent extraction is an equilibrium process and it is controlled by the distribution law, not by the amount of solvent or solute.

mcqs.q: Which factor does NOT control solvent extraction, according to the lesson?
options: The equilibrium between the two liquids
The distribution of solute between liquids
mcqs.why: The lesson lists the amount of solvent used as a wrong option; solvent extraction as an equilibrium process is controlled by the distribution law instead.

mcqs.q: Solvent extraction is particularly useful for separation when the product is:
options: Non-volatile or thermally stable in all cases
Volatile or thermally unstable in all cases
mcqs.why: The marked answer states solvent extraction is particularly useful when the product to be separated is non-volatile or thermally unstable.

mcqs.q: Why is solvent extraction preferred for a thermally unstable product?
options: Because the product is non-volatile or thermally unstable and suits this technique
Because the product must be boiled strongly
Because the product is always a gas
Because no solvent is needed for it
mcqs.why: The lesson identifies non-volatile or thermally unstable products as the case where solvent extraction is a particularly useful separation technique.

mcqs.q: In paper chromatography, the comparative rates at which solutes move depend on what?
options: Size of the chromatographic tank used
mcqs.why: The lesson marks Rf values of solutes as the factor on which the comparative rates at which the solutes move in paper chromatography depend.

mcqs.q: What does an Rf value determine in paper chromatography, according to the lesson?
options: The size of the paper needed
The size of the tank needed
The boiling point of the solvent
The comparative rate at which a solute moves
mcqs.why: The notes tie the movement of solutes in paper chromatography to their Rf values, so Rf determines the comparative rate at which each solute moves.

lessons.title: Fill in the Blanks
lessons.notes_html:
2(i). A complete chemical characterization of a compound must include both qualitative and quantitative analyses.

2(ii). During filtration the tip of the stem of the funnel should touch the side of the beaker to avoid splashing.

2(iii). A fluted filter paper is used to speed up the process of filtration.

2(iv). A solvent used for crystallization is required to dissolve ______ of the substance at its boiling point and ______ at the room temperature. A solvent used for crystallization is required to dissolve a large amount of the substance at its boiling point and only a small amount at room temperature, so that crystals separate on cooling.

2(v). Repeated solvent extractions using small portions of solvent are more efficient than using a single extraction with larger volume of the solvent.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A complete chemical characterization of a compound must include both ____ and ____ analyses.
mcqs.why: The fill in the blanks lesson completes this sentence with qualitative and quantitative analyses, both being required for complete characterization.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: During filtration the tip of the stem of the funnel should touch ____ to avoid splashing.
mcqs.why: The lesson states the tip of the stem of the funnel should touch the side of the beaker to avoid splashing during filtration.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A ____ filter paper is used to speed up the process of filtration.
mcqs.why: The lesson fills this blank with fluted, stating a fluted filter paper is used to speed up the process of filtration.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A crystallization solvent must dissolve ____ of the substance at its boiling point.
mcqs.why: The completed sentence in the lesson says the solvent is required to dissolve a large amount of the substance at its boiling point.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A crystallization solvent must dissolve ____ of the substance at room temperature.
mcqs.why: The lesson completes this part by stating only a small amount dissolves at room temperature, in contrast to the large amount at boiling point.

mcqs.q: What happens on cooling a hot solution in a good crystallization solvent?
mcqs.why: The lesson explains the solubility difference means crystals separate on cooling, because less substance can remain dissolved at the lower temperature.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: Repeated solvent extractions using ____ portions of solvent are more efficient.
mcqs.why: The lesson states repeated solvent extractions using small portions of solvent are more efficient than using a single extraction with larger volume.

mcqs.q: Which extraction method does the lesson say is less efficient?
options: A single extraction with a larger volume of solvent
Extraction repeated until solute is recovered
mcqs.why: The lesson contrasts the methods and states the single extraction with larger volume is less efficient than repeated extractions with small portions.

mcqs.q: For complete characterization, which analysis identifies what is present and which measures how much?
options: Only qualitative is required for both jobs
Only quantitative is required for both jobs
Qualitative identifies and quantitative measures, and both are required
mcqs.why: The opening blank of the lesson requires both qualitative and quantitative analyses together for a complete chemical characterization of a compound.

mcqs.q: The purpose of touching the funnel stem to the beaker side, as stated in the lesson, is to avoid what?
mcqs.why: The lesson gives splashing as the thing avoided by keeping the tip of the funnel stem touching the side of the beaker during filtration.

lessons.title: True or False
lessons.notes_html:
3(i). Tick the correct sentences. If the sentence is incorrect, write the correct statements. (i) A qualitative analysis involves the identification of elements present in a compound. Correct. Qualitative analysis identifies which elements are present in a compound.

3(ii). If the process of filtration is to run smoothly, the stem of the funnel should remain empty. Incorrect. Correct statement: If the process of filtration is to run smoothly, the stem of the funnel should remain continuously full of liquid (not empty), so that a gentle suction is developed.

3(iii). If none of the solvents is found suitable for crystallization a combination of two or more immiscible solvents may be used. Incorrect. Correct statement: If none of the solvents is found suitable for crystallization, a mixture of two or more miscible solvents (not immiscible solvents) may be used.

3(iv). A solute distributes itself between two immiscible liquids in a constant ratio of concentrations depending upon the amount of solvent added. Incorrect. Correct statement: A solute distributes itself between two immiscible liquids in a constant ratio of concentrations at a given temperature, independent of the amount of solvent added (the distribution law).

3(v). Paper chromatography is a technique of partition chromatography. Correct. In paper chromatography the stationary phase is water adsorbed on the paper and the solute partitions between this water and the mobile organic solvent, so it is a partition chromatography.

mcqs.q: What does qualitative analysis involve, according to the corrected statements?
options: Identification of elements present in a compound
Measurement of the exact mass of a compound
Separation of crystals from a solution
mcqs.why: The lesson marks as correct that a qualitative analysis involves the identification of elements present in a compound, that is what elements are present.

mcqs.q: For filtration to run smoothly, the stem of the funnel should remain in what state?
options: Continuously full of liquid, not empty
mcqs.why: The corrected statement says the stem should remain continuously full of liquid, not empty, so that filtration runs smoothly and suction develops.

mcqs.q: Why should the funnel stem remain full of liquid during filtration?
options: So that crystals form in the stem
So that a gentle suction is developed
So that the paper dries quickly
mcqs.why: The correction in the lesson explains the full stem is needed so that a gentle suction is developed, which keeps the filtration running smoothly.

mcqs.q: If no single solvent is suitable for crystallization, what may be used?
options: A combination of two or more immiscible solvents
A mixture of two or more miscible solvents
mcqs.why: The corrected statement says a mixture of two or more miscible solvents may be used, and the original immiscible version is marked incorrect.

mcqs.q: The statement 'immiscible solvents are combined when no single crystallization solvent is suitable' is:
options: Incorrect, the solvents combined must be miscible
mcqs.why: The lesson marks the immiscible version incorrect and corrects it to miscible solvents, which can mix to give a suitable combined solvent.

mcqs.q: A solute distributes itself between two immiscible liquids in what kind of ratio?
options: A ratio depending on the amount of solvent added
A ratio that changes every minute
A constant ratio of concentrations at a given temperature
A ratio equal to the volumes used
mcqs.why: The corrected distribution law statement says the ratio of concentrations is constant at a given temperature for a solute between two immiscible liquids.

mcqs.q: The distribution ratio of a solute between two immiscible liquids is independent of what?
options: The temperature being given and fixed
mcqs.why: The lesson corrects the statement to say the constant ratio is independent of the amount of solvent added, depending instead on the given temperature.

mcqs.q: Paper chromatography is a technique of which type of chromatography?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks as correct that paper chromatography is a technique of partition chromatography, because the solute partitions between two phases.

mcqs.q: In paper chromatography, what is the stationary phase?
options: The organic solvent moving up the paper
The paper fibres themselves as a liquid
mcqs.why: The lesson explains the stationary phase is water adsorbed on the paper, and the solute partitions between this water and the mobile organic solvent.

mcqs.q: In paper chromatography, between which two phases does the solute partition?
options: Water adsorbed on paper and the mobile organic solvent
mcqs.why: The lesson states the solute partitions between the water on the paper and the mobile organic solvent, which is why it is partition chromatography.

lessons.title: Short Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q4. Why is there a need to crystallize the crude product?

A crude product contains impurities: soluble impurities, insoluble impurities and

coloured matter, together with unchanged starting material. Crystallization purifies

it because, on cooling a hot saturated solution, the pure substance separates as

crystals while the impurities stay dissolved in the mother liquor (or are removed by

filtration), giving a pure, well-defined product of a definite melting point.

Q5. A water insoluble organic compound aspirin is prepared by the reaction of

salicylic acid with a mixture of acetic acid and acetic anhydride. How will you

separate the product from the reaction mixture?

Aspirin is insoluble in water, whereas acetic acid and the excess acetic anhydride

(which hydrolyses to acetic acid) are water-soluble. Pour the reaction mixture into

cold water: aspirin separates as a solid. Filter it off, wash it with cold water to

remove the acid, dry it, and recrystallize it from a suitable solvent (for example

aqueous ethanol) to obtain pure aspirin.

Q6. A solid organic compound is soluble in water as well as in chloroform. During its

preparation, it remains in aqueous layer. Describe a method to obtain it from this

layer.

Use solvent extraction in a separating funnel. Shake the aqueous layer repeatedly

with small portions of chloroform: the compound distributes itself between water

and chloroform and passes into the chloroform layer. Separate the lower chloroform

layer each time, combine the extracts, and evaporate the chloroform (the solvent is

volatile) to leave the solid compound behind.

Q7. The figure shows a developed chromatogram on paper with five spots: (i)

Unknown mixture X (ii) Sample A (iii) Sample B (iv) Sample C (v) Sample D. Find out

(i) the composition of unknown mixture X (ii) which sample is impure and what is its

composition.

Spots are identified by their height above the base line, that is, by their Rf value: a

component of the mixture gives a spot at exactly the same height as the same pure

sample. (i) The unknown mixture X shows two spots, one at the height of sample A

and one at the height of sample C. Composition of X: A + C. (ii) Sample D shows two

spots, one at the height of sample B and one at the height of sample C, although D

was supposed to be a single substance. Sample D is therefore impure; its

composition is B + C. Samples A, B and C each show a single spot and are pure.

Q8. In solvent extraction technique, why repeated extraction using small portions of

solvent are more efficient than using a single extraction but larger volume of

solvent?

By the distribution law, each extraction removes a fixed fraction of the solute

remaining in the aqueous layer. With several small portions, the solute is partitioned

afresh each time, so the total fraction removed is larger than with one large portion

of the same total volume, where after the first (and only) equilibrium a large

fraction can remain behind in the water layer. Repeated small extractions therefore

recover more solute.

Q9. Write down the main characteristics of a solvent selected for crystallization of a

compound.

A good crystallization solvent must: (1) dissolve a large amount of the substance at

its boiling point but only a small amount at room temperature; (2) not react

chemically with the substance; (3) dissolve the impurities either very well (so they

stay in the mother liquor) or very poorly (so they can be filtered off hot); (4) give

well-defined crystals on cooling; (5) be easily removed from the crystals (volatile)

and be cheap and safe to use.

Q10. You have been provided with a mixture containing three inks with different

colours. Write down the procedure to separate the mixture with the help of paper

chromatography.

Procedure: (1) Draw a base line near the bottom of a strip of chromatography paper

and put a small spot of the ink mixture on it, keeping the spot above the solvent

level. (2) Hang the strip in a closed tank so that its lower end dips in a suitable

solvent (the mobile phase), with the spot above the solvent. (3) The solvent rises by

capillary action; each ink component partitions between the water on the paper and

the solvent and moves at its own rate (its own Rf value). (4) When the solvent front

has risen far enough, remove the strip, mark the solvent front at once, and let it dry.

(5) Three separate coloured spots appear at different heights, one for each ink, and

each can be identified by comparing its Rf value with that of a known ink.

mcqs.q: Why is there a need to crystallize a crude product?
options: It contains impurities, so crystallization purifies it and pure crystals separate on cooling
It contains no impurities at all
Crystallization changes it into a different compound
It is needed only to colour the product
mcqs.why: The notes say a crude product contains soluble and insoluble impurities and coloured matter, and on cooling the pure substance separates as crystals while impurities stay in the mother liquor.

mcqs.q: Aspirin is insoluble in water while acetic acid and acetic anhydride are soluble. How is aspirin separated?
options: Heat the mixture until aspirin evaporates
Pour the mixture into cold water, aspirin separates as a solid and is filtered off
Add more acetic anhydride to dissolve aspirin
mcqs.why: The notes describe pouring the reaction mixture into cold water so aspirin separates as a solid, which is then filtered, washed with cold water and dried.

mcqs.q: After filtering crude aspirin, how is it purified further in the notes?
options: It is burnt to remove impurities
It is kept dissolved in acetic acid
It is recrystallized from a suitable solvent such as aqueous ethanol
It is mixed with chloroform and discarded
mcqs.why: The notes state the filtered aspirin is recrystallized from a suitable solvent, for example aqueous ethanol, to obtain pure aspirin.

mcqs.q: A compound soluble in water and chloroform remains in the aqueous layer. How is it obtained?
options: By filtering the aqueous layer through paper only
By boiling the water until it colours
By solvent extraction, shaking the aqueous layer repeatedly with small portions of chloroform in a separating funnel
mcqs.why: The notes use solvent extraction in a separating funnel, shaking repeatedly with chloroform so the compound passes into the chloroform layer.

mcqs.q: In the chloroform extraction described, which layer is the chloroform layer that is separated each time?
options: The solid layer on the filter
mcqs.why: The notes say to separate the lower chloroform layer each time, combine the extracts, and evaporate the volatile chloroform to leave the solid compound.

mcqs.q: Why are repeated extractions with small portions of solvent more efficient?
options: One large portion removes a fixed fraction many times
Small portions change the distribution law
Each extraction removes a fixed fraction of the solute remaining, so several small portions remove more in total
mcqs.why: By the distribution law each extraction removes a fixed fraction of what remains, so partitioning afresh with several small portions recovers more solute than one large portion.

mcqs.q: Which is a main characteristic of a good crystallization solvent?
options: It reacts chemically with the substance
It dissolves the same amount at all temperatures
It can never be removed from crystals
It dissolves a large amount at its boiling point but only a small amount at room temperature
mcqs.why: The notes list this solubility behaviour first among the characteristics of a solvent selected for crystallization of a compound.

mcqs.q: Which is another required characteristic of a crystallization solvent in the notes?
options: It must not react chemically with the substance
It must react strongly with the substance
It must be non-volatile and hard to remove
It must dissolve impurities poorly in every case
mcqs.why: The notes require that the solvent not react chemically with the substance, dissolve impurities very well or very poorly, and be easily removed from crystals.

mcqs.q: In the chromatogram described, unknown mixture X shows spots at the heights of samples A and C. What is X?
options: A mixture of B and C
A mixture of A and C
mcqs.why: Spots are identified by height, that is Rf value: X has one spot at the height of A and one at the height of C, so the composition of X is A plus C.

mcqs.q: Sample D shows two spots at the heights of B and C although it was supposed to be one substance. What is D?
options: Impure, with composition A and C
Impure, with composition B and C
mcqs.why: The notes conclude sample D is impure because it shows two spots, one at the height of B and one at the height of C, while A, B and C each show a single spot.

lessons.title: Key Facts
lessons.notes_html:
Facts to Remember

  • The product PV has the S.I. unit of joule (energy).
  • Total kinetic energy = (3/2) nRT. Moles: O2 = 8/32 = 0.25 mol; H2 = 8/2 = 4 mol. At the same temperature, total K.E. ratio = 0.25 : 4 = 1 : 16.
  • Smell of the cooking gas during leakage from a gas cylinder is due to the property of diffusion of gases.
  • Equal volumes of ideal gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules (Avogadro's law).
  • The temperature above which a substance exists only as a gas is called critical temperature.

mcqs.q: What is the S.I. unit of the product PV for a gas?
mcqs.why: The notes state that the product PV has the S.I. unit of joule, which is the unit of energy.

mcqs.q: What is the total kinetic energy of n moles of an ideal gas at temperature T?
mcqs.why: The notes give total kinetic energy = (3/2) nRT, so it depends on the amount of gas and the absolute temperature.

mcqs.q: How many moles are present in 8 g of O2? (molar mass of O2 = 32 g/mol)
mcqs.why: Moles = mass / molar mass, so 8 / 32 = 0.25 mol, exactly as worked out in the notes for oxygen.

mcqs.q: How many moles are present in 8 g of H2? (molar mass of H2 = 2 g/mol)
mcqs.why: Moles = mass / molar mass, so 8 / 2 = 4 mol, exactly as worked out in the notes for hydrogen.

mcqs.q: 8 g each of O2 and H2 are kept at the same temperature. What is the ratio of their total kinetic energies (O2 : H2)?
mcqs.why: At the same temperature total K.E. is proportional to moles: O2 has 0.25 mol and H2 has 4 mol, and 4 / 0.25 = 16, so the ratio is 0.25 : 4 = 1 : 16.

mcqs.q: The smell of cooking gas spreads during leakage from a cylinder due to which property of gases?
mcqs.why: The notes state that the smell of cooking gas during leakage from a gas cylinder is due to the property of diffusion of gases.

mcqs.q: According to Avogadro's law, equal volumes of ideal gases at the same temperature and pressure contain:
options: Equal number of atoms in every case
mcqs.why: The notes state Avogadro's law as: equal volumes of ideal gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.

mcqs.q: The temperature above which a substance exists only as a gas is called:
mcqs.why: The notes define the critical temperature as the temperature above which a substance exists only as a gas.

mcqs.q: For a fixed mass of gas in a cylinder at constant temperature, Boyle's law says that:
mcqs.why: The piston diagram in the notes illustrates Boyle's law, P x V = constant, at constant temperature for a fixed mass of gas.

mcqs.q: At the same temperature, 4 mol of H2 and 0.25 mol of O2 are compared. Which sample has the greater total kinetic energy?
options: The O2 sample, because oxygen is heavier
The O2 sample, because it has fewer moles
The H2 sample, because it has more moles
mcqs.why: Total K.E. = (3/2) nRT, so at the same temperature it grows with n: 4 mol gives far more than 0.25 mol, and 4 / 0.25 = 16 times as much.

lessons.notes_html:

Q1(ix). Gases deviate from ideal behaviour at high pressure. Which of the following is
correct for non-ideality?

Q1(xi). A real gas obeying van der Waals equation will resemble ideal gas if
A. both 'a' and 'b' are large
✓ B. both 'a' and 'b' are small
